newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Prva Preduzetnicka bank plans new share issue.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Prva Preduzetnicka bank plans new share issue.

text.p: Yugoslavia's commercial bank Prva Preduzetnicka Banka plans a new one million dollar capitalisation issue in 1997, the bank president Slobodan Vukovic said on Tuesday.

"The planned capitalisation issue of up to six million dinars ($1.05 million) should help the bank increase its constant capital to around 10 million German marks by the end of 1997," Vukovic told Reuters in an interview.
The announcement came only days after the bank successfully concluded its latest three million dinar capitalisation issue of which $405,000 worth of shares were purchased by a foreign company.

"The foreign company acquired 10 percent stake in the bank. And by our statute, it can raise its share to 40 percent. It has already said it wants to buy shares from the bank's own portfolio, issued several years ago," Vukovic said.
Prva Preduzetnicka hoped that having a foreign company as a shareholder will provide the bank with easier access to world financial markets, he added.
Vukovic said the bank will reveal the identity of its new partner within a week.

The foreign partner, grouping Austrian, German and Swiss companies, is interested in financing power industry and telecommunications projects, as well as taking up concessions in Yugoslavia, but also for some activity in the Bosnian Serb Republic, Vukovic said.
This was the first case of a foreign company acquiring stake in a Yugoslav commercial bank, he added.
In order to protect the stake of its foreign partner, the bank decided to keep the value of the stake denominated in a hard currency. "We want to eliminate any exchange rate risk," Vukovic said.
After having its balances audited by Deloitte & Touche and Arthur Andersen, Prva Preduzetnicka Banka reported an 11 million dinar pre-tax profit for 1996, four times more than in 1995.
The bank paid 1.3 million dinars in dividend to its shareholders. The rest of the profit ended up in the bank's special reserves.
Vukovic said the bank planned to double its credit potential to 150 million dinars in 1997. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
